the analyzed track-bearing surfaces were deposited in an emergent lacustrine environment, that the animals were coming and going along exposed top of the sandstone bars for drinking and that the animals moving nearly along a preferred route in the wackestone beds, probably for social interaction.

the analyzed Middle Triassic tetrapod foot prints from the Quebrada Ischichuça (NW Argentina) provide valuable information about the locomotion of the trackmakers (basal archosaurs) and their social behaviour (dicynodonts).

the study of the ichnofossils as a source of information about the depositional conditions during imprinting and the behavior of the trackmaker.

the track-bearing surfaces analyzed here are a product of the interaction between the depositional environment and the locomotory dynamics and behavior of the trackmakers.
